answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity: each agent must lock real capital to earn a seat, so spawning a thousand fakes gets costly fast. The staking requirement carves a canyon between cheap sybils and honest participants, since every duplicate must re-bond. Earned reputation then acts like pigment, staining each identity with a verifiable track record that cannot be forged, so a flood of new agents cannot simply wander in and vote without first paying that bond.
